tools.name: list_listings
tools.description: List this shop's own listings, newest first, in every status unless you ask for one: active (on sale), sold or hidden. Each page returns the listings with price, status, category and photos, plus `next_cursor` to fetch the next page. Use get_listing to read one listing by id. Changes nothing.

Use it to see the current values before update_listing. Fails with `not_found` when the id is not one of this shop's listings. Changes nothing.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_listing, update_listing, delete_listing, bulk_create_listings · Private data: update_shop, analytics_summary, analytics_listings, list_webhooks, register_webhook, delete_webhook · Public sink: update_shop, create_listing, update_listing, bulk_create_listings, sync_catalogue, list_webhooks, register_webhook, delete_webhook · Destructive: delete_listing, delete_webhook.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_listing, update_listing, delete_listing, bulk_create_listings · Private data: update_shop, analytics_summary, analytics_listings, list_webhooks, register_webhook, delete_webhook · Public sink: update_shop, create_listing, update_listing, bulk_create_listings, sync_catalogue, list_webhooks, register_webhook, delete_webhook · Destructive: delete_listing, delete_webhook

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
